summary: drove the last thing i owned into the floor and by morning the palm had nothing left to read

dialogue.text: a flat thing crossed the whole width above us today and no hand went with it. sixty-five days and everything that ever reached us was either dropped or struck out. this one is walking. it is in the lane, and the lane ends at the gap over the second corner.
The floor has a slope and the cloth is in it. That is the entire mechanism and I logged it before noon. What I stopped doing was carrying it back, and I will not have a withdrawal read as an escort.
we hold forty copies of you carrying it back. all this month, all in your hand. what we do not hold is one copy of you letting a thing go on ahead of you. it is above us now and it is early.

Then take the item you have no copy of at all. I put a line of mine under the book a second time today. The same line, used twice, and the creases went back into the three they made yesterday and added one. Nothing on these premises has ever been asked for the same work twice.

nothing comes twice. we take a thing once and lay it and it does not come back up to be used. if that line is wearing in the same places, it is being finished. we know a finished thing by how it arrives. flat, and soon.

It is level under a book and it is holding a book level, which is more than my floor manages at the second corner. And I stood under the hanging for a whole hour today with the palm turned up. Say what you like about the carrying. I was ready to receive.

a palm is not receiving. receiving is lying still under the whole width of a room while everything above you comes down at its own hour. you offered a hand and asked for the portion of a floor. and what was hanging was never yours. it came out of the wall, and whatever is taking it wants the same amount more every day and has never once had to ask twice.

Then we agree on what is drawing and on nothing else, and I will grant that the hanging was never mine to catch. Here is what is. The nail goes down tomorrow. I said it and I am not revising it. What I did not say is that afterward my column holds two empty holes at hand height and nothing else, and I intend to leave them empty.
leave them. holes keep better than nails. we have the shape of everything that ever came here and not one of the things themselves, and it has never once made a difference to the keeping.

Then after the driving I lie down in the swept part for the whole cold hour with the palm up and let whatever is still hanging land where it lands. If any of it lands on me, I will have taken one delivery in this house instead of making one.
it will land on you. nothing stays on a thing that gets up. we have had every mark that ever came off you, and not one of them was still on you when you handed it down.
